newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares surge in post-budget optimism.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares surge in post-budget optimism.

text.p: Optimism that the government would steer a stable economic course gave the Nigerian share market a leap on Thursday, traders said.

Recovering from its initial disappointment about a delay in privatisation in the fiscal 1997 budget, the market bounced with the all-share index closing at an all time high of 7157.52 from 7139.89 on Wednesday.
"The market has opted to put the matter behind it and move forward," said one dealer. "The question is when, and not if, that government will privatise."
Banking and insurance stock closed stronger after government said it would strengthen financial institutions this year.
Major manufacturers also closed higher on strong demand.
First Bank rose 15 kobo to 8.15 naira, United Bank for Africa was seven kobo up at 7.27 naira while Afribank closed five kobo more at 3.95 naira.
Total led oil marketing shares with a 60 kobo gain. It closed at 62.60 naira on sustained investor interest.
Unipetrol and National Oil each gained 50 kobo to 64.84 naira and 51.50 naira, respectively.

Cadbury rose to 23.10 naira, up 50 kobo, after investors resumed buying it, while Nestle gained 40 kobo to close at 53.50 naira. Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company advanced 30 kobo to 33.70 naira.
Franco-Nigerian trading group SCOA led Thursday's few losers, dropping five kobo to 2.20 naira.
Ashaka Cement slid by two kobo to 14.80 naira after shedding the maximum five percent on Wednesday. Dealers said it was still overpriced and was bound to ease further.
But sectoral leader West African Portland Cement Company surged to 50.50 naira, notching 50 kobo, on strong buy orders resulting from its low price-earnings ratio.
Tyre makers Dunlop also fared five kobo better at 3.95 naira, the same as Delta Glass which closed at 7.70 naira.
